On July 13, 2026, Gov.
Henry McMaster appointed Darline Graham to the U.S.
Senate vacancy caused by Lindsey O.
Graham’s death; the certificate was laid before the Senate on July 14, 2026.
State law set a special Republican primary for August 11, 2026, a runoff if needed on August 25, and kept the general election on November 3, 2026; her appointment runs until January 3, 2027.

Between 1960 and 1989, Pew reported 29 appointees sought election and 11 won (38%), a weaker record than the post-1990 period.

polymarket-631045.brief: The question asks whether the Republican nominee wins the Florida U.S. Senate special election on 3 November 2026, with resolution on a unanimous call by the Associated Press, Fox News and NBC or else certification. The Florida Division of Elections lists appointed incumbent Ashley Moody (Republican), Angie Nixon (Democrat) and Neil Gillespie (no party affiliation) as qualified (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp?OfficeCode=USS&elecID=20261103-GEN, quotes not found on page). In 2024 Republican Rick Scott won with 5,977,706 votes (55.6%) to Democrat Debbie Mucarsel-Powell's 4,603,077 (42.8%) (https://results.elections.myflorida.com/SummaryRpt.asp?DATAMODE=&ElectionDate=11%2F5%2F2024&Race=FED, quotes checked). In 2022 Marco Rubio won 57.7% to Val Demings's 41.3%. The base rate is two of two recent Senate generals won by Republicans. As of 30 September Florida had 5,678,755 active Republican and 4,133,397 active Democratic registrants, a gap of about 1.55 million, whereas Democrats led in 2020 (https://dos.fl.gov/elections/data-statistics/voter-registration-statistics/voter-registration-reports/voter-registration-by-party-affiliation, 2026-10-12, quotes checked). A New York Times/Siena poll of 19-26 October had Moody at 50% and Nixon at 44% (https://floridapolitics.com/archives/827512-nyt-poll-shows-ashley-moody-crossing-50-line-byron-donalds-with-narrow-lead/, 2026-10-28, quotes checked). A St. Pete Polls survey of 25-27 October had Moody at 49% and Nixon at 45%, narrowing to 47% to 46% when reweighted to the registration split (https://floridapolitics.com/archives/827489-final-st-pete-polls-ashley-moody-holds-49-to-45-over-angie-nixon-with-a-cushion-that-shrinks-if-republicans-stay-home/, 2026-10-28, quotes checked). A Division of Elections compilation through 28 October showed 594,296 Republican and 727,616 Democratic mail ballots and 972,753 Republican and 788,137 Democratic early ballots (https://countyfilesvbm-ev.floridados.gov/VoteByMailEarlyVotingReports/PublicStats, 2026-10-29, quotes not found on page). Republicans have historically cast a larger share of their votes on Election Day. What would change the answer: Election Day turnout by party or independents breaking strongly toward Nixon.

On the Florida Division of Elections candidate list for the November 3, 2026 general election, Ashley Moody (REP), marked incumbent, and Angie Nixon (DEM) are both listed as Qualified and as having Won their primaries; Neil J.
Gillespie (NPA) is listed as Qualified.

As of September 30, 2026, Florida had 5,678,755 active registered Republicans and 4,133,397 active registered Democrats (13,672,122 total).
On the same series, Democrats still led on September 30, 2020 (5,315,954 to 5,218,739).

The Division of Elections compilation timestamped 1:03 p.m.
on October 29, 2026, for the November 3, 2026 general election, and cumulative only through the prior day, showed 594,296 Republican and 727,616 Democratic voted mail ballots, and the statewide early-vote row showed 972,753 Republican and 788,137 Democratic early ballots (early total 2,210,593).

In the official November 5, 2024 Florida results, Republican Rick Scott received 5,977,706 votes (55.6%) and Democrat Debbie Mucarsel-Powell 4,603,077 (42.8%) for U.S.
Senate.

In the official November 8, 2022 Florida results, Republican Marco Rubio received 4,474,847 votes (57.7%) and Democrat Val Demings 3,201,522 (41.3%) for U.S.
Senate.

A St.
Pete Polls survey of 916 likely voters fielded October 25–27, 2026, and published October 28, had Moody at 49% and Nixon at 45% (margin of error ±3.2 points); the same story said reweighting to the registration split produced 47% to 46%.
A New York Times/Siena poll of 813 Florida voters conducted October 19–26, 2026, published October 28, had Moody at 50% and Nixon at 44%, with a reported margin of error of 3.9 points.
